idea.title: Adversarial Strategy to Sway Responses in Knowledge Retrieval Systems
idea.purpose: This work addresses the vulnerability of knowledge-enhanced language models to stealthy poisoning threats aimed at altering generated viewpoints.
idea.mechanism: The approach reverse-engineers the underlying search component using surrogate training to craft subtle document triggers that transfer effectively to target systems.
idea.evaluation: It is tested by measuring the attack success rate, the directional shift in generated opinion polarity, and user cognition changes across four domains.

source.title: Improving Retrieval-Augmented Generation through Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

idea.title: Cooperative Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Information Retrieval and Generation Pipelines
idea.purpose: This work addresses the problem of component misalignments in retrieval-augmented generation pipelines when they are optimized separately.
idea.mechanism: It treats each component in the pipeline as an independent agent in a cooperative multi-agent reinforcement learning framework, jointly optimizing them toward a shared final answer quality reward.
idea.evaluation: Experiments on various question-answering benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed joint optimization approach boosts overall performance and outperforms existing baselines.

source.title: QuIM-RAG: Advancing Retrieval-Augmented Generation With Inverted Question Matching for Enhanced QA Performance

idea.title: Improving Document Based Answer Generation Through Query Alignment and Indexing
idea.purpose: This work addresses information dilution and hallucinations in knowledge integration frameworks when handling large text corpora for answering queries.
idea.mechanism: It generates potential queries from document chunks and constructs an inverted index matching strategy to retrieve the most relevant text segments for response generation.
idea.evaluation: The approach is compared against traditional retrieval models using semantic similarity and generation evaluation metrics on a custom website corpus with ground truth data.

source.title: SaLoRA: Safety-Alignment Preserved Low-Rank Adaptation

idea.title: Preserving safety alignment during parameter efficient adaptation of language models
idea.purpose: This work addresses the issue where adaptation techniques inadvertently compromise the safety alignment of language models during task-specific tuning.
idea.mechanism: It introduces a fixed safety module derived from safety data combined with targeted initialization for trainable adaptation parameters.
idea.evaluation: Experiments are conducted to compare the approach against various adapter baselines across multiple tasks and metrics.

source.title: TriAdaptLoRA: Brain-Inspired Triangular Adaptive Low-Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning

idea.title: Brain-Inspired Dynamic Matrix Factorization for Efficient Language Model Adaptation
idea.purpose: Current parameter reduction techniques struggle with suboptimal capacity allocation and inflexible dimensionality management during model training.
idea.mechanism: It divides transformation matrices into specialized components, assesses parameter importance using norm metrics, and dynamically adjusts internal dimensions throughout the learning process.
idea.evaluation: It is tested on various language understanding and generation tasks to demonstrate superior performance and computational efficiency.

source.title: Structure-Learnable Adapter Fine-Tuning for Parameter-Efficient Large Language Models

idea.title: Optimizing Modular Network Insertion and Routing for Efficient Multi-Task Adaptation
idea.purpose: This work addresses parameter redundancy and inflexible routing in modular network updates for large language models.
idea.mechanism: It introduces learnable gating functions and sparsity controls to dynamically optimize module placement and activation pathways during training while keeping the core network frozen.
idea.evaluation: It is evaluated on multiple multi-task language understanding benchmarks to measure accuracy, compression, and robustness against noise.

idea.title: Building an Expert Assistant for Materials Science Using Graph and Vector Queries
idea.purpose: This work addresses the challenge of systematically retrieving and reasoning over unstructured scientific text that suffers from inconsistent terminology and scattered experimental data.
idea.mechanism: We implement and compare two query pipelines, one using semantic vector embeddings and another using a structured knowledge graph, to provide context-preserving information to a language model.

idea.title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation via Utility-Based Information Consolidation for Transformers
idea.purpose: Transformers fail to retain critical information over extended inputs and waste computation during inference adaptation.
idea.mechanism: A selective controller estimates the informational value of input segments and restricts gradient updates to high-utility regions.
idea.evaluation: Experiments on long-sequence evaluation suites demonstrate superior performance with fewer gradient steps compared to uniform update baselines.

idea.title: Evaluating Extended Audio Memory Limits in Spoken Dialogue Systems
idea.purpose: This work addresses the lack of evaluations for audio-based models handling extended conversational histories where critical information is easily forgotten.
idea.mechanism: It constructs a benchmark that extends audio history across multiple turns and durations, featuring fine-grained provenance annotations and varying semantic complexity.
idea.evaluation: It tests several representative audio models to measure how performance degrades as the required historical evidence is placed further back in the dialogue.

idea.title: Evaluating Extended Text Attribution Abilities in Large Language Models
idea.purpose: This work addresses the underexplored capability of attributing items to specific sections across extensive textual inputs.
idea.mechanism: It introduces a benchmark suite containing synthetic and realistic subsets that require identifying document indices associated with a target key.
idea.evaluation: Thirteen advanced language models are tested on this benchmark, accompanied by human evaluations, format adjustments, fine-tuning, and error analyses.

source.title: Behavior-Adaptive Q-Learning: A Unifying Framework for Offline-to-Online RL

idea.title: Bridging offline and online reinforcement learning via behavior-adaptive regularization
idea.purpose: This work addresses the poor performance and instability of policies learned from static data when transitioning to online fine-tuning in dynamic environments.
idea.mechanism: It introduces a dual-objective loss function that leverages an implicit behavioral model to align the online policy with the offline data distribution when uncertainty is high, gradually relaxing the constraint as reliable experience accumulates.
idea.evaluation: The approach is tested across standard reinforcement learning benchmarks, demonstrating improved robustness, faster recovery, and higher overall performance compared to prior baselines.

source.title: Offline RL with Smooth OOD Generalization in Convex Hull and its Neighborhood

idea.title: Improving offline reinforcement learning via smooth value generalization in out-of-distribution regions
idea.purpose: This work addresses the over-constraint issue and value overestimation caused by distributional shifts in offline reinforcement learning.
idea.mechanism: The approach introduces a modified Bellman operator that updates out-of-distribution values by smoothing them with neighboring in-sample values within a safety-guaranteed neighborhood.
idea.evaluation: The method is evaluated on standard offline reinforcement learning benchmark suites against existing state-of-the-art algorithms.

source.title: Belief-Based Offline Reinforcement Learning for Delay-Robust Policy Optimization

idea.title: Transformer-Based Belief Prediction for Latency-Resistant Offline Reinforcement Learning
idea.purpose: This work addresses the problem of offline reinforcement learning agents failing when deployed in environments with action and observation latencies not present in the static training logs.
idea.mechanism: It uses a sequence model to predict a belief state over past histories, generating stable actions under delays despite being trained only on delay-free data.
idea.evaluation: Experiments across various delay settings on standard simulation benchmarks demonstrate improved performance compared to baseline history-augmentation methods.

source.title: Do Counterfactually Fair Image Classifiers Satisfy Group Fairness? - A Theoretical and Empirical Study

idea.title: Investigating the Relationship Between Counterfactual Fairness and Group Fairness in Images
idea.purpose: This work clarifies whether satisfying counterfactual fairness ensures group fairness in image classification tasks.
idea.mechanism: We theoretically analyze how latent correlated attributes break the implication and empirically evaluate both fairness notions on newly constructed image evaluation datasets.
idea.evaluation: Extensive experiments on newly built image benchmarks demonstrate how reducing reliance on correlated latent attributes helps counterfactual fair models satisfy group fairness.

idea.purpose: This work investigates how the presence of duplicated images in training sets impacts the generalization and accuracy of vision models.
idea.mechanism: The study empirically analyzes model performance under various scenarios of uniform and non-uniform data duplication across standard and robust training pipelines.
idea.evaluation: It is evaluated by measuring the training efficiency and classification accuracy of networks trained on datasets containing varying levels of duplicate images.

source.title: Mitigating Clever Hans Strategies in Image Classifiers through Generating Counterexamples

idea.title: Correcting Spurious Correlations in Visual Classifiers Using Generated Counterexamples
idea.purpose: This work addresses the vulnerability of deep models to spurious correlations when group labels are absent and data is scarce.
idea.mechanism: It generates diverse counterexamples to let annotators correct decision boundaries via knowledge distillation, enriching undersampled groups without needing confounder labels.
idea.evaluation: The approach is evaluated across five datasets ranging from synthetic tasks to an industrial application, measuring generalization improvements and robustness.

idea.title: A Benchmark for Assessing Automated Judges of Multi-Step Agent Trajectories
idea.purpose: The high cost of human annotation for complex agent tasks creates a bottleneck, while the reliability of automated judges remains unmeasured.
idea.mechanism: We collected a public collection of process-level critiques generated by language model judges on various agent tasks, paired with detailed human quality labels.
idea.evaluation: We tested several judge models and reasoning configurations against human annotations to measure their alignment on error location and reasoning quality.

source.title: BayesJudge: Uncertainty-Aware Bayesian Meta-Evaluation of Human and LLM Judgments

idea.title: Online Bayesian Aggregation of Conflicting Rater Decisions and Position Biases
idea.purpose: The approach addresses the problem of noisy and conflicting pairwise preference decisions from multiple unreliable human and automated judges.
idea.mechanism: It uses an online probabilistic inference framework that jointly estimates underlying item quality alongside rater confusion matrices and presentation-order biases.
idea.evaluation: The framework is tested through controlled synthetic simulations and evaluated on a benchmark summarization dataset to verify parameter recovery and bias detection.

source.title: LLM-as-a-Judge: Rapid Evaluation of Legal Document Recommendation for Retrieval-Augmented Generation

idea.title: Evaluating Automated LLM Judges for Legal Information Retrieval Systems
idea.purpose: This paper investigates how to reliably use large language models as automated judges for evaluating specialized document retrieval systems.
idea.mechanism: The study analyzes different inter-rater reliability metrics and statistical tests to determine which ones robustly capture alignment with human assessments and enable sound system comparisons.
idea.evaluation: It is evaluated through systematic experimentation comparing various agreement metrics and statistical tests on evaluation data.
